title: I2C Start Bit and Address Framing
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Learning MicroPython
description: Step through a 13-event I2C transaction between a controller, an EEPROM at 0x50 and an LCD backpack at 0x27 to see why the start bit, not the byte value, decides whether a device is being addressed.

educational.topic: I2C Start Bit and Address Framing
learningObjectives: Explain why an I2C device checks an incoming byte against its own address only immediately after a start bit or repeated start.
Trace a complete I2C transaction (start, address, ACK, data bytes, repeated start, stop) and identify what each bus event means.
Explain why a second device on the same bus cannot confuse another device's data bytes with its own address.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Step-through worked example with synchronized code highlighting
keyQuestions: When does a device compare an incoming byte to its own address?
Why can't the EEPROM's memory-address bytes be mistaken for the LCD's device address?
commonMisconceptions: Students often assume every byte on the bus is checked against every device's address, rather than only the byte immediately after a start bit.
